rows.title: CT budget panel mulling whether to challenge Lamont’s guardrails
rows.standfirst: The Appropriations Committee will have to choose this week whether to take on Lamont or deny funding boost for higher ed and social services.

rows.title: Leaders now say they can fix CT budget without adding big dollars
rows.standfirst: Budget transfers could still help CT’s core programs, but Gov. Lamont would have to bend ‘fiscal guardrails’ to make the Democrats’ plan work.

rows.title: With tax changes off the table, CT finance panel focuses on studies
rows.standfirst: The legislature’s tax writing committee now hopes to launch analyses of existing tax breaks and options to bolster CT’s competitiveness.

rows.title: Finance panel OKs bills to attack poverty, boost child care in CT
rows.standfirst: The CT legislature’s finance committee adopted measures to fight poverty and backed a 5-year $674 million capital building program for UConn.

rows.title: Panel backs new CT budget with built-in shortfalls, few details
rows.standfirst: The CT Appropriations Committee would bolster higher education and social services but ignore pension and revenue problems in its budget plan.

rows.title: Lamont won’t help lawmakers leave gaps in next CT budget
rows.standfirst: If Democratic legislators want more funds in core programs, they must close holes in the CT budget as well, the Lamont administration said.

rows.title: Budget panel OKs 2.5% raise for most CT state workers
rows.standfirst: The raises, which the full legislature is expected to vote upon before the regular session ends May 8, would cost more than $190 million.

rows.title: CT officials insist tax cuts will remain as pandemic relief expires
rows.standfirst: Despite a projected $16B income tax revenue loss across CT and 25 other states, Lamont and the legislature agree CT tax cuts aren’t at risk.

rows.title: Lamont won’t say if he’ll ease ‘debt diet’ to make CT budget fix work
rows.standfirst: CT legislative leaders plan to borrow to cover operating expenses in the next budget — creating a significant hole to be tackled next year.

rows.title: Legislature OKs 2.5% raise plus step hike for most CT employees
rows.standfirst: Analysts say the raises will cost CT about $190 million next fiscal year. Raises go into effect July 1 and a step hike on Jan. 1.

rows.title: House GOP budget: Boost K-12, cut care for undocumented
rows.standfirst: House Republicans pitched a budget that boosts education, ends health care for undocumented women and children and trims the state workforce.

rows.title: Lamont defends fiscal guardrails but is open to workarounds
rows.standfirst: A shared desire to end the session without drama has led to a deal with some budget gimmicks.

rows.title: CT revenues soaring, but legislators still can’t spend them
rows.standfirst: Progressives have said this year’s budget debate, which involved huge piles of untouchable cash, will fuel the push for reforms in 2025.

rows.title: Report: Billions more in taxes coming in to CT than expected
rows.standfirst: Citing ‘shocking … revenue numbers,’ House Speaker Matt Ritter said ‘there might need to be an adjustment’ to how much CT saves.
